newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London gave up much of their modest gains by the close after a day of thin trading. December ended 50 points higher at $316.70, while March closed unchanged at $313.50 per tonne. In New York raw sugar futures closed largely unchanged after the most-active March contract struggled and then failed to reach resistance seen at 10.80 cents/lb. Overall activity was dull with no fresh news to report. March ended 1 point higher at 10.66 cents/lb, while May remained flat at 10.70 cents/lb. The back months closed unchanged to 1 point higher.

UKRAINE - As was to be expected official sources in the Ukraine now said that beet sugar production could turn out to be below 3 million at 2.8 million tonnes, white value, which compares to earlier expectations of a crop of 3.2 million tonnes. Last year's production was 3.485 million tonnes. The fall in production was ascribed to adverse weather conditions.

RUSSIA - 796 000 ha of sugar beet (about 79 per cent of total plantings) had been harvested by October 21, compared with 881 000 ha at the same date last year. Harvesting has made good progress everywhere although it is still lagging behind that of last year. This reflects favourable harvesting conditions. Unusually dry and warm weather favoured the harvest in most regions, particularly in the Central European part. As a result of the favourable weather conditions, yields have stabilized and production could be slightly higher than expected. It is now believed that sugar beet production in 1996 will reach 17 million tonnes, still 11 per cent less than last year and the lowest output for the last 40 years after 1993.

MAURITIUS - Mauritius produced 119,535 tonnes of sugar, raw value, in July 1996, significantly up on last year's figure of 64,589 tonnes. This brought total production in the first two months of 1996/97 (June/May) up to 130,711 tonnes which compares to 82,416 tonnes produced the same two months in 1995. Total production in 1996 is estimated at 646,173 tonnes, raw value, up from 571,515 tonnes produced the previous year. The country exported 78,552 tonnes, raw value, in June/July 1996, 6.5 per cent more than was exported the same two months in 1995. As usual the main country of destination in June/July 1996 was the UK with 74,394 tonnes, up from 71,037 tonnes the same two months in 1995. TENDERS

The European Union awarded 44,750 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 45.512 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on Wednesday. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to October 23 reached 706,650 tonnes, which compares to 920,525 tonnes last year.
